land.text: the island of Crete, from which 'the International Squadron and the occupying forces ashore expelled all Ottoman forces ... in November 1898'

predecessors.note: Ottoman suzerainty continued de jure ('autonomous state of the Ottoman Empire'); Cliopatria's Ottoman shape 1895-1899 still contains part of Crete, so 1898-1899 overlap in Cliopatria. The Cretan Revolt (1897-1898) precedes the state and is not listed in wars: Colonel Vassos landed at Kolymbari on 16 February 1897, the powers announced autonomy under Ottoman suzerainty on 20 March 1897 and blockaded the island from 21 March, and the infobox gives 'Cretan victory; Ottoman withdrawal from Crete; Establishment of the Cretan State' (Cretan Revolt page, read 2026-10-25); the Ottoman forces were expelled in November 1898 and the state was founded in December 1898.

land.text: the island of Crete: 'unilateral union with Greece' on 7 October 1908, 'annexed de facto in 1908 and de jure in 1913'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Greek shape includes Crete from 1908. The union was recognised by the Great Powers only in 1913 (Treaty of London 30 May 1913; Greek flag raised at Firka, Chania, 1 December 1913).

keyframe_review.note: Area check: the Cretan State page gives no area, the Crete page gives 'an area of 8,450 km2' in the lead (8,336 km2 in the body). Cliopatria's polygon is 5,499 km2, 0.65 of the island (0.66 of the body figure); the gazetteer resolves it to 16 cells (about 4,046 km2) against 27 cells (about 6,828 km2) for the admin-1 Kriti, so the polygon covers about 60 percent of the island while the page says the state governed 'the island of Crete'. Verdict adjust to the whole of Kriti. Cliopatria's Ottoman shape 1895-1899 also still holds part of Crete in 1898-1899 (me-10 to fix).

keyframe_review.note: Same polygon as the 1898 shape (5,499 km2 in both rows): no territorial event in 1905 on the page, which dates only the Therisos revolt (23 March 1905) and the September 1906 replacement of Prince George by Zaimis. Same correction as 1898.

correction.text: the whole island of Crete until the unilateral union with Greece on 7 October 1908

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Cretan State row ends in 1907 and its Greek shape holds Crete from 1908, but the page dates the union to 7 October 1908 (infobox), so the Cretan State is alive for the first nine months of 1908. The renderer should hand Crete to the First Hellenic Republic at the dissolve event.

ledger.note: 1898: the Cretan State is founded under Ottoman suzerainty. 'founded when Prince George of Greece and Denmark arrived to take office as the first high commissioner', 21 December 1898 (9 December Julian; the infobox 'Proclamation: 9 December 1898'); the Ottoman forces had been expelled in November 1898 and the Admirals Council was dissolved on 26 December 1898.

region.text: the island of Crete, an 'autonomous state of the Ottoman Empire'

ledger.note: 1898: the Cretan State is an autonomous state under Ottoman suzerainty. Infobox 'Status: Autonomous state of the Ottoman Empire'; the lead has the state governing Crete from 1898 to 1913 'under de jure suzerainty of the Ottoman Empire but with de facto independence secured by European Great Powers'. The Powers' presence: six Great Powers sent warships in February 1897 (the International Squadron) and soldiers of five of them 'arrived to occupy key Cretan cities in late March and April 1897'; Germany withdrew in November 1897 and Austria-Hungary in March 1898, and after Prince George was replaced in September 1906 'the withdrawal of the foreign troops began' (no date for the last departure). That garrison is the guarantee of the autonomy, not a separate control level, so it is not an occupation event. Mirrors the vassal pair that the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should carry instead of its 1900 loss of Crete. Added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-18-h).

region.text: the island of Crete: unilateral union with Greece

ledger.note: 1908: the Cretan deputies end the Ottoman link by proclaiming union with Greece. Infobox 'Unilateral union with Greece: 7 October 1908'. The sultan's formal rights lapsed later: 'Sultan Mehmed V relinquished his formal rights to the island' in May 1913 (Treaty of London, infobox 30 May 1913), and the formal union followed on 1 December 1913. Confidence 2: the October 1908 date is the page's, but the Ottoman side kept its de jure rights to 1913 (the vassal_end follows the de facto break and the Cliopatria Greek shape). Added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25 (reviewer eu-18-h).

region.text: the island of Crete: unilateral union with Greece

ledger.note: 1908: the Cretan deputies proclaim union with Greece. Infobox 'Unilateral union with Greece: 7 October 1908'; the Greek flag replaced the Cretan, officials swore an oath to King George I and Greek laws were enacted. Not recognised internationally until the Treaty of London (30 May 1913) and the Greek flag at Firka on 1 December 1913; the lead dates the state 'from 1898 to 1913'.

wars.name: Therisos revolt
wars.outcome: Venizelos and his supporters gathered at Therisos near Chania (infobox 'Theriso revolt: 23 March 1905'); in September 1906 Prince George was replaced by Alexandros Zaimis, Greek officers began replacing Italians in the Gendarmerie and foreign troops began to withdraw.
wars.note: No land was held apart from the state, so no rebel dossier and no contest event; the page does not date the end of the revolt.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border. The unrecognised union of 1908 does not change the outline.

notes: Dates: the Cretan State page gives the state 'from 1898 to 1913' (lead) but 'annexed de facto in 1908 and de jure in 1913'. identity.end is the unilateral union of 7 October 1908 because Cliopatria's Greek shape includes Crete from 1908 and the Greek administration took over (Greek flag, laws, oath to King George I); the formal end of Ottoman rights is 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London) and 1 December 1913 (Greek flag at Firka). A reviewer who prefers 1913 should keep the shape and move the dissolve event; no border changes either way. Founding: the page gives both 13 December (Prince George's arrival) and 21 December 1898 (founding) in different places; the infobox says Proclamation 9 December 1898 (Julian). The ledger uses December 1898. Area: the page gives no area; the Cliopatria polygon (5,499 km2, 16 gazetteer cells) is smaller than the island (admin-1 Kriti, 27 cells), hence verdict adjust for all shapes. Ottoman side: Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire shape 1895-1899 still contains part of Crete (16 cells in 1897, 0 from 1900); the me-10 dossier should drop Crete in 1898 (suzerainty only, as a vassal/autonomous state). The Ottoman suzerainty over the Cretan State is not recorded as a vassal_start here (that event belongs to the suzerain's dossier). Great Power occupation of Crete (1897 onwards, five powers' troops; withdrawal begun after 1906) is not dated on the pages opened and is not recorded as an occupation event. The Greco-Turkish War (1897; declared 17 April 1897 per the Cretan Revolt page) predates the state and is not listed in wars. Page budget: 2 pages (Cretan State, Cretan Revolt 1897-1898); the Greco-Turkish War page and the Crete page (area) were not opened.
